newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP coal shipments up 2.8 pct in 9 months.
newsitem.headline: BHP coal shipments up 2.8 pct in 9 months.

text.p: Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) said on Wednesday its total coal shipments in the nine months to February 28 rose by 2.8 percent to 37.96 million tonnes.
Shipments rose by 5.5 percent to 13.46 million tonnes in the latest three months to February 28.
Shipments by the Central Queensland Coal Associates (CQCA) joint venture from five Queensland mines in the nine months rose by 5.2 percent to 20.24 million tonnes.
In the February quarter, shipments from CQCA mines edged up by 0.4 percent to 6.79 million tonnes.

Nine-month shipments from the Gregory joint-venture mine in Queensland fell by 3.7 percent to 2.12 million tonnes, but showed strong growth in the three months to February in rising by 28.8 percent to 933,000 tonnes.

Shipments by BHP Mitsui Coal from three Queensland mines in the nine months fell by 5.8 percent to 5.74 million tonnes after falling by 19.6 percent to 1.83 million tonnes in the three months to the end of February.
Shipments from BHP's total Queensland operations in the nine months rose by 2.1 percent to 28.10 million tonnes after falling by 2.1 percent to 9.55 million tonnes in the February quarter.
Shipments from the Mount Owen mine in New South Wales jumped to 842,000 tonnes from 266,000 tonnes in the nine months, after rising to 698,000 tonnes from 16,000 tonnes in the latest quarter.
BHP's New South Wales Collieries operations shipped 4.68 million tonnes in the nine months, down by 7.4 percent, after a 16.2 percent rise to 1.81 million tonnes in the February quarter.
BHP's Indonesian operations shipped 6.9 percent more coal at 4.34 million tonnes in the nine months after a 1.4 percent decline to 1.41 million tonnes in the latest quarter.

Japan took 10.21 million tonnes in the nine months, down from 10.45 million in the corresponding period a year ago, Europe took 8.22 million tonnes, up from 7.92 million tonnes, while other markets took 19.53 million tonnes, up from 18.54 million tonnes.
